meta.title: The Harbour Letter
meta.purpose: Example story for the Narrative State Engine. This state was written first; the prose in manuscript/ was written to realise it, so the answers here are true by construction.
meta.story_key: Sortable story-time coordinate. Negative means before the story opens. A scene's key is its entry point; whatever happens during the scene sits just above it. Equal keys mean the order is not established.
meta.tell: Position in the telling (reading order), 1 to 12. Scene 8 is a flashback: late in the telling, early in story time.

scenes.story_label: The night of 30 April, six months earlier (flashback)

propositions.text: Edmund Kessler died on the night of 30 April.
The harbour office ledgers show a monthly withdrawal marked R.P., running for about thirty years and stopping in January.
Marta has been taking money from the business.
The R.P. withdrawals were made on Edmund's instructions.
R.P. is Rose Pike, and the withdrawals were payments Edmund made to her every month.
Rose Pike died in January.
Jonas Pike is Edmund Kessler's son.
Edmund wrote a private letter, sealed and stamped it, and never posted it.
The letter is addressed to Jonas Pike.
Sarah took the letter from Edmund's desk drawer on the night he died.
Sarah has had the letter in her keeping since April.
There was nothing in Edmund's desk but invoices.
Sarah has never opened the letter.
In the letter, Edmund acknowledges Jonas as his son and gives him a half share in the harbour office.
The man in the grey coat is Jonas Pike.
The man in the grey coat is Rose Pike's son.
The man who came to the office on Tuesday was only a traveller asking about ferry times.
Edmund gave the letter to Sarah himself.
Edmund had decided not to send the letter.
propositions.note: Ambiguous by design. Characters hold opinions; the story never decides.

propositions.text: Edmund wrote the letter before his last quarrel with Daniel.
propositions.note: Not established. The two events have tied story keys.

propositions.text: Edmund left no letter or message for Rose Pike's son.
A man in a grey coat came to the harbour office on Tuesday asking for Edmund Kessler.
A man in a grey coat has been watching the harbour office from the quay.
Jonas Pike is in town.
Hallam Marine's offer for the harbour office lapses on Friday the twenty-third.
Daniel means to sell the harbour office.
The R.P. withdrawals are connected with the name on the envelope.
Before she died, Rose Pike told Jonas that Edmund Kessler was his father.
Sarah is keeping a sealed envelope in Edmund's handwriting hidden from Daniel.
propositions.note: A concealment is derived: Sarah has the letter (P11) and Daniel does not know it until scene 7.

propositions.text: Daniel believes Marta has been taking money from the business.
Daniel believes Edmund gave the letter to Sarah himself.
Edmund and Daniel quarrelled about selling the office in the last week of April.
Rose Pike had a son by Edmund Kessler.
propositions.note: Split from P07. The reader learns this in scene 5 without the name; that the son is called Jonas Pike (P07) is not stated until scene 10. One proposition cannot carry two facts with different reveal times.

propositions.text: Jonas Pike is Rose Pike's son.
propositions.note: What is given away if Marta says "Rose's boy" aloud.

propositions.text: Sarah was at her father's desk in the harbour office on the night he died.
propositions.note: A circumstance of P10 that can be given away on its own.

propositions.text: The letter lay in Edmund's desk drawer until the night he died.
propositions.note: A circumstance of P10 that can be given away on its own.

events.summary: Edmund begins paying Rose Pike every month through the office books; Marta makes the payments and keeps the record.
Rose Pike tells Jonas that Edmund Kessler is his father.
Rose Pike dies; the payments stop.
Edmund writes, seals and stamps a letter to Jonas Pike and leaves it in his desk drawer.
Edmund and Daniel quarrel about selling the office.
Edmund collapses at the office and is taken to hospital.
Fetching her father's glasses from the office at night, Sarah finds a sealed, stamped envelope under the invoices in his desk drawer and reads the name on it.
events.quote: under them, flat against the wood, was an envelope

events.summary: The hospital rings Sarah: her father has died.
events.quote: your father died a few minutes ago

events.summary: Sarah puts the envelope inside her coat and takes it away.
events.quote: She put the envelope inside her coat.

events.summary: Daniel, Marta and Tom learn that Edmund has died.
Sarah goes back to the city with the letter hidden in the lining of her suitcase.
Going through thirty years of ledgers, Daniel finds a monthly withdrawal marked only R.P. that stops in January.
Daniel asks Marta what R.P. is. She says the payments were his father's instructions and will say no more.
Daniel concludes that Marta has been taking the money.
Alone in the kitchen, Sarah takes a sealed envelope from the lining of her suitcase and hides it in the old tea tin.
events.quote: She laid the envelope in the tea tin

events.summary: Over supper Daniel tells Sarah that money is missing from the books, that he means to sell, and when Hallam's offer lapses.
Prompted by the solicitor, Daniel asks Sarah what was in their father's desk. She says there was nothing but invoices. Tom, in the doorway, hears it.
Daniel tells Sarah that Marta has been robbing them and shows her the R.P. entries. Sarah says she does not believe it.
A man in a grey coat comes into the office asking for Edmund Kessler. Marta, visibly shaken, tells him Edmund died in April. He leaves without giving a name.
Tom asks who the man was. Marta says he was a traveller who wanted the ferry times, and tells Tom not to trouble Daniel with it.
At home Marta goes through thirty years of payment stubs, thinks over who the visitor was, and resolves to say nothing yet.
Sarah takes the envelope from the tea tin and carries it in her coat pocket to the post office, meaning to post it. She does not.
From the north quay Sarah sees a man in a grey coat watching the harbour office. They look at each other from a distance; he goes into the Ship Hotel.
events.quote: A man in a grey coat

events.summary: Sarah tells Daniel she has had a letter of their father's for months and lays the sealed envelope on the table. Daniel reads the name on it.
Sarah will not say where she got it. Daniel assumes their father gave it to her, and she lets that stand. He wants to open it; she refuses and keeps it.
As agreed overnight, Daniel locks the letter unopened in the office safe until Monday. Marta sees the envelope and reads the name on it.
events.quote: He shut the safe and turned the key

events.summary: Daniel tells Marta that Sarah has been carrying the letter since April.

Daniel tells Marta that auditors are coming on Monday, making his suspicion of her plain, and leaves. Sarah asks Marta whether she knows who the man on the envelope is; Marta says to ask her on Monday.
events.quote: The auditors are coming on Monday.

events.summary: Alone with Daniel, Marta shows him thirty years of payment stubs and tells him who Rose Pike was and that Jonas is his father's son. Daniel sees she took nothing.
At her father's grave Sarah finds the man in the grey coat. He tells her his name is Jonas Pike.
Jonas tells Sarah what his mother told him before she died, and that he came to the office on Tuesday and learned Edmund was dead.
Sarah tells Jonas that her father left a letter for him that was never posted, and asks him to come to the office on Monday.
Sarah brings Jonas into the office and introduces him as their father's son. Tom recognises him as Tuesday's visitor. Daniel says Marta already told him.
events.quote: That's the fellow who wanted the ferry times

events.summary: Daniel sends Tom out, opens the safe and hands the letter to Jonas.
events.quote: Daniel sent Tom out to the yard and shut the door.

events.summary: Jonas opens the letter and reads it aloud: Edmund acknowledges him and gives him a half share in the harbour office.
Marta says Edmund stamped it and meant it to go. Sarah says he never posted it and nobody will ever know what he meant.

embargoes.note: That Edmund has another son. The reader gathers it in scene 5; Daniel and Sarah learn much later.
That the son is the Jonas Pike on the envelope. The reader can infer it from scene 7; it is stated in scene 10.
The name on the envelope. Sarah knows it from April; the reader first sees it in scene 7.
How Sarah came to have the letter. Daniel never learns it.
That the stranger and the name on the envelope are the same man.
What the letter says. Nobody living knows until it is read.

secrets.note: How Sarah came by the letter. She tells nobody in the story as written, and Daniel is left believing their father gave it to her. Declared here so that 'never learns it' is a fact and not just a missing record.

rules.text: Whether Edmund meant to send the letter is ambiguous by design. No scene may settle it. Characters may hold and voice opinions.
Whether the letter was written before or after the quarrel is not established. Do not establish it without an author decision.
Close third person, past tense, one point-of-view character per scene. British spelling. The narration reports only what the POV character can perceive or think.
